Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `testMySqlNullOutput` in the `CSVPrinterTest` class is testing the output of null values in MySQL format using `CSVPrinter`. The test creates an array containing the values "NULL" and null, sets up the CSV format to be MySQL-compatible, writes the array to a CSV file using the printer, and then compares the generated output with the expected output.

The current bug report indicates that there is an issue with how the nullString is handled in CSV output. Specifically, the nullString "NULL" is being escaped as "\\N" instead of being handled as expected. The suggestion is to modify `CSVPrinter` to not escape the nullString value.

Looking at the failing test, it seems that the issue is related to how null values are processed and escaped in the CSV output, especially when using a specific nullString value and MySQL-compatible format.

Next, we need to locate the part of the code in `CSVPrinter` responsible for handling null values, especially the nullString, to identify where the escaping of nullString may be occurring incorrectly.
